reconcile.connective: Defenders read “face to face” as the directness of the speaking, not a visible form — so 5:4 and 4:12 describe one event without conflict.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the plainest reading: 4:12 says they saw no form at all, yet 5:4 says God talked with them face to face — the same author cannot have it both ways.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (“Did the Israelites see God face to face on Mount Horeb?” / “Can God be seen?”)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); skepticsannotatedbible.com

excerpts.excerpt_text: not in a visible and corporeal form, of which there was no trace (Deu 4:12, Deu 4:15), but freely, familiarly, and in such a manner that no doubt could be entertained of His presence.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles the two verses: reads 5:4 “face to face” as familiar/direct speech, not visual perception, and cites 4:12/4:15 as proof that no form was seen — the exact tension of this contradiction.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Deuteronomy 4:12 and 5:4
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D harmonize this exact pair on the passage: at 5:4 they argue “face to face” (בּפנים פּנים) “simply denotes the directness with which Jehovah spoke to the people,” not a visible form, and at 4:12 they reconcile “Ye heard the sound of the words, but ye did not see a shape” with the texts denying any sight of God's form.
